title: Large Scale Applications of Machine Learning using Remote Sensing for Building Agriculture Solutions (NASA ARSET)
provider: NASA Applied Remote Sensing Training (ARSET), NASA Applied Sciences / Earthdata
language: English (live delivery). Slides for all three parts also provided in Spanish. No Russian materials.
cost: Free ($0). ARSET trainings are free and open; registration required.
certificate: Certificate of completion available but conditional: per ARSET policy you must attend ALL live webinar sessions AND submit the homework (Google Form) by the due date (April 1, 2024). Recordings-only does not qualify. Certificates emailed ~2-4 months after the course concludes.
duration: Three parts of 1.5 hours each = 4.5 contact hours, delivered weekly on March 5, 12 and 19, 2024. Each part offered twice the same day (10:00-11:30 or 14:00-15:30 EST). Plus optional self-paced exercises and one homework assignment.
format: Live instructor-led online webinar series (not self-paced). Recordings, slides, data files, and Q&A transcripts published afterward for asynchronous review.
target_audience: Remote sensing scientists, practitioners, and geospatial analysts from local, regional, federal, and non-governmental organizations who use remote sensing for agriculture; also agronomists, data scientists, data engineers, and ML engineers. Advanced prerequisites required (see assessment/notes).

syllabus.topics: Submitting boundary lists to the USDA NASS API and retrieving Cropland Data Layer (CDL) rasters; manipulating Sentinel-2 imagery; verifying data through visualization; Databricks environment setup. Instructors: Sean McCartney (ARSET) with John Just & Erik Sorensen (John Deere/Deere & Co.). Slides in EN+ES, data files, Q&A transcript, Databricks setup guide, optional exercise.

Setting up a TensorFlow data loader that reads Parquet files to build a training pipeline; data normalization; time-series bucketization; train/validation/test splitting with random sampling that avoids information (data) leakage. Slides EN+ES, data, Q&A transcript, optional exercise.

Setting up and training a 1-D convolutional neural network (CNN) to detect crop type from time-series spectral data; monitoring hyperparameters during training; validating predictions on the test set. Slides EN+ES, data, Q&A transcript, optional exercise.

assessment: Three optional, ungraded, self-paced exercises (one per part). One graded homework assignment submitted via Google Form, due April 1, 2024 — required (together with full live attendance) for the certificate. Heavy prerequisite chain: learners must first complete 'Fundamentals of Remote Sensing' plus several SAR/optical crop-classification trainings (Agricultural Crop Classification with SAR/Optical RS; Mapping Crops/Biophysical Characteristics with Polarimetric SAR; Crop Mapping using SAR/Optical RS).
hands_on: Strong applied focus. End-to-end big-data ML pipeline on agricultural imagery: (1) pull CDL labels via NASS API + Sentinel-2 imagery for >5GB-scale areas; (2) build a TensorFlow data loader over Parquet, normalize, bucketize time series, split without leakage; (3) train and validate a 1-D CNN crop-type classifier. Work runs in Databricks notebooks with PySpark; data files and per-part optional exercises supplied. NOT free/zero-cost to reproduce — requires AWS S3 + Databricks compute.
tools: Python; TensorFlow (model + data loaders); PySpark (distributed processing); Databricks (notebook/compute environment); AWS S3 (cloud storage); Parquet (columnar data format); USDA NASS API. Datasets: Sentinel-2 optical imagery and the USDA Cropland Data Layer (CDL) as labels. Note: does NOT use Google Earth Engine or Colab — it is an AWS/Databricks/PySpark/TensorFlow stack.
strengths: Realistic, production-grade end-to-end ML workflow (ingest -> data loader -> train -> validate) rather than a toy example
Co-taught with industry practitioners from John Deere, grounding it in real agricultural ML practice
Explicitly teaches large-scale (>5GB) data handling and, importantly, how to avoid information/data leakage in train/val/test splits — a rigor point most intro courses skip
Uses authentic agricultural labels (USDA CDL via NASS API) paired with Sentinel-2 — a clean labeled-data pattern
Free, with persistent published slides (EN + ES), data, Q&A transcripts, and recordings for asynchronous reuse
Time-series spectral 1-D CNN for crop-type classification is a strong, transferable modeling pattern
weaknesses: Stack is NOT zero-cost: AWS S3 + Databricks require paid cloud accounts — directly conflicts with FOLUR's $0 / no-admin invariant (Colab/GEE)
Uses neither Google Earth Engine nor Colab, so the hands-on pedagogy does not transfer directly to FOLUR's tooling
Advanced level with a heavy prerequisite chain (Fundamentals + multiple SAR/optical trainings) — too steep for SMB agro practitioners
US-centric data: USDA CDL and NASS API have no Kazakhstan/Central Asia equivalent, so labels must be substituted
Short (4.5 contact hours) and assumes substantial prior Python/ML maturity; little conceptual scaffolding for non-coders
Certificate requires live attendance on fixed 2024 dates — not reusable asynchronously for a credential
